title: TCS Adds Staff and Guards Pay Cycle; Wipro Cuts 6,716 Jobs and Rules Out Another Hike
excerpt: The September quarter split India's IT majors on people: TCS hired 4,258 net and recruited for AI skills, while Wipro shrank its workforce, credited AI productivity, and said no further salary increase is under consideration.
body:
• TCS added 4,258 employees net in the September quarter to reach 598,056 and onboarded 10,000 freshers; Wipro cut 6,716 staff to 236,328, its biggest quarterly decline in recent quarters.
  • On pay, the two firms split: Wipro CHRO Saurabh Govil said the salary increase rolled out in March 2026 stands and another hike is not under consideration, while TCS trimmed its quarterly variable-pay outlay for July-September instead of freezing base pay.
  • AI is driving the divergence: about 80% of TCS's September-quarter additions carried new-age skills and 25-30% had specialised AI skills, while Wipro says AI has freed capacity equivalent to 20,000 workers, who were redeployed.
  • The results gap matches: TCS net profit rose 15% year on year to Rs 13,884 crore with $9.6 billion in deal wins, while Wipro profit fell 1.9% to Rs 3,201 crore as large-deal bookings dropped 58.6% to $0.7 billion.

India's two IT services majors reported September-quarter results within eight days of each other and described two different workforces. Tata Consultancy Services is hiring again, tilting recruitment toward artificial intelligence skills and protecting its pay cycle. Wipro is smaller than it was in June, says AI productivity is doing work that once needed people, and has closed the door on another salary increase for now.

Headcount: one expanding, one shrinking

TCS added 4,258 employees net in the July-September quarter, taking its workforce to 598,056, and onboarded about 10,000 freshers. It was the company's third consecutive quarter of net additions, a turnaround from FY26, when headcount shrank by roughly 24,000 in a restructuring aimed at mid-to-senior roles. CHRO Sudeep Kunnumal said TCS had issued about 25,000 campus offers at the start of the fiscal year and is in the final stages of campus hiring for the next graduating class, according to The Peoples Board's account of the results.

Wipro moved the other way. Its headcount fell 6,716 in the quarter to 236,328 from 243,044, reversing a gain of 888 in the June quarter. The company onboarded only about 1,000 freshers in the entire first half and plans to return to campuses in the second half, with most intake landing in the March quarter. It hired about 7,500 freshers in FY26 and intends to hold annual intake near that level, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Attrition was 13.8% at Wipro, 13.3% at TCS.

Pay: a closed door at Wipro, a squeezed bonus at TCS

The pay contrast is sharper than the hiring contrast. Wipro restarted salary increments only on March 1, 2026, ending a pause stretching back to its previous cycle in September 2024, PeopleMatters reported. On the September-quarter earnings call, Govil confirmed that increase is the last one on the table: another hike is not under consideration right now. TCS chose a different lever. CFO Samir Seksaria told analysts the company had set a lower outlay for performance-linked bonuses, citing performance against internal targets, after paying mid-to-senior staff an average of 60-70% of variable pay in the June quarter, down from up to 80% in the two quarters before, Moneycontrol reported. TCS held its operating margin at 24%.

AI is redrawing both workforces, from opposite ends

Both companies put AI at the centre of their people strategy, but the arithmetic runs in opposite directions. TCS is hiring into the technology: COO Aarthi Subramanian said nearly 80% of the employees added in the September quarter had new-age technology skills and 25-30% had specialised AI skills, a mix the company intends to maintain. CEO K Krithivasan said AI work accounted for 10% of TCS revenue in the quarter, within total contract value of $9.6 billion, according to PeopleMatters. Wipro is using AI to need fewer people per unit of work: its AI initiatives have lifted productivity by the equivalent of about 20,000 employees, who were redeployed rather than replaced, CTO Sandhya Arun told Reuters, with more than 100,000 staff given advanced AI training. Govil credited direct productivity from AI projects as one factor in the quarter's headcount decline.

The scoreboard behind the split

The financial results explain the room each company has. TCS posted net profit of Rs 13,884 crore, up 15% year on year, on revenue of Rs 73,188 crore, and declared a Rs 12 per share dividend. Wipro's net profit fell 1.9% year on year to Rs 3,201 crore even as revenue rose 9.1% to Rs 24,752 crore; IT services revenue was flat in constant currency, total bookings fell 22.9% to $2.6 billion, and guidance for the December quarter is a decline of 1.5% to growth of 0.5% in constant currency. Wipro's IT services margin improved 50 basis points to 16.5%, helped by the smaller wage bill. The next test arrives in January, when Wipro's second-half campus hiring shows in its headcount and both firms report whether AI-led demand is converting into growth.
